text:
jess (support): heads-up — multiple Dedicated customers started filing latency complaints around 09:30 UTC. p95/p99 for some pools jumped sharply and we're seeing attach timeouts + intermittent 504s. pasting a snippet from one customer: 

olivia (cust): attach latency timeline: 09:25 1.2s, 09:30 4.8s, 09:32 12.1s, 09:34 30.7s -> errors: "gpu init: cuda init timeout" and "attach handshake failed". model: open-llm/7b, pool: dedicated-eu-3

maria (sre): thanks. can you confirm pool id (looks like dedicated-eu-3). any recent deploys to Dedicated kernels or infra updates? also need request ids and sample request headers.

kyle (platform): we did push inference-kernel:v3.4.2 to Dedicated pools at 09:10 UTC to address memory fragmentation. rollout id: rl-2026-03-17-002. it changed the GPU driver init path + deferred cuda warmup during attach (intended to reduce cold mem usage).

noah (oncall): that change lines up with the regressions. probable that deferred warmup + pool pre-warm set to 0 = cold GPU starts on attach -> high p95/p99. can we bump capacity and force pre-warm while we investigate?

maria (sre): executing immediate mitigations. steps: 
1) scale up dedicated-eu-3 by +2 replicas (temporary)
2) set pool prewarm.workers=2
3) route affected customer traffic to hosted fallback for 30m if errors persist
command I'm running: 
```
redwoodctl pool scale --pool dedicated-eu-3 --delta 2 --reason "emergency latency mitigation"
redwoodctl pool update-config --pool dedicated-eu-3 --set prewarm.workers=2
```

devops-bot: scale request accepted: sr-8812, new target replicas=6 (in progress)

kyle (platform): digging into the v3.4.2 change — we introduced a lazy cuda init to reduce startup memory but it appears to introduce longer driver handshake on some instance types (nvidia-a100-p4 topology). also noticed a config override removed pre-warm for that pool during a customer-specific patch last week.

jess (support): customer-facing note: opened a ticket and informed customer we're investigating and have temporarily routed their requests to hosted (they accepted). please keep me posted on ETA so I can update SLAs.

deploy-bot: rolled back inference-kernel to v3.4.1 for pool dedicated-eu-3 (rollback id rb-3145)

maria (sre): monitoring: after scale + rollback + pre-warm change: p95 for dedicated-eu-3 down from 3.1s -> 1.2s; p99 down from 8.7s -> 2.3s. error rate (attach timeout) fell from 4.6% -> 0.3% in 15m window. leaving rollback + pre-warm for now.

kyle (platform): root cause hypothesis: v3.4.2 lazy-init + pool-specific prewarm override => thundering cold attach on burst traffic -> high p99. action items: 
- revert lazy-init behavior or gate it behind instance-type safe list (kyle)
- add deploy-time perf smoke (fast attach) to Dedicated rollout pipeline (maria/kyle)
- audit pool config overrides and restore pre-warm defaults (platform)
- follow-up postmortem + customer RCA (noah)

noah (oncall): timeline action: create incident ticket INC-2026-03-17-08, schedule 30m postmortem sync at 11:00 UTC, assign owners as above.

jess (support): updated customer — they noted improvement and appreciate the quick failover. will keep case open until postmortem provided. :thumbsup:

maria (sre): leaving mitigation in place for 2h, will monitor p99 and snapshot heap/kernel logs. if numbers stay stable we'll plan a controlled reinstate of v3.4.2 behind canary with attach-smoke checks.

kyle (platform): I'll also add an invariant check to the deploy pipeline: any kernel change that alters init path must run attach latency smoke for 1h on a dedicated canary pool before fleet rollout.

jess (support): thanks all. closing customer-facing update. please add any further notes to INC-2026-03-17-08.

-- end thread --
